answer: Agents earn influence only after completing tasks whose results are independently checked by randomly assigned peers; each check requires a small bond that is forfeited for dishonest approval. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting into sybils does not multiply trusted weight. To evade the checks, an attacker must fund many bonds and sustain convincing work across accounts, paying real resources for each identity. The pigment marks a submission, the trellis links its review history, and the crystal records settled trust.
